title: CogSys: Efficient and Scalable Neurosymbolic Cognition System via Algorithm-Hardware Co-Design
problem: Neurosymbolic AI workloads—combining neural network inference with symbolic reasoning (e.g., probabilistic logic, abduction)—exhibit high memory intensity, compute heterogeneity, and irregular access patterns that cause severe underutilization on commodity CPU/GPU/TPU hardware.
motivation: Neurosymbolic AI offers superior data efficiency and interpretability for edge deployments, but lacks dedicated hardware support, preventing its adoption in real-time cognitive applications that require reasoning within human-level latency constraints.
method: CogSys is an algorithm-hardware co-design framework with three layers: (1) Algorithm: an efficient tensor factorization technique to reduce the compute and memory footprint of symbolic reasoning operations; (2) Hardware: a scalable ASIC architecture with reconfigurable neuro/symbolic processing elements (nsPEs) and a bubble streaming (BS) dataflow with spatial-temporal (ST) mapping that enables highly parallel, pipelined execution of heterogeneous neural and symbolic kernels; (3) System: an adaptive workload-aware scheduler (adSCH) that orchestrates the assignment of neural vs. symbolic kernels to nsPEs for high resource utilization, evaluated under TSMC 28nm.
key_novelty: Reconfigurable nsPE tiles with bubble streaming dataflow that unify neural and symbolic computation in a single spatial architecture with adaptive kernel scheduling, enabling real-time abductive reasoning for the first time.
contributions: First characterization of neurosymbolic workload bottlenecks on existing hardware (CPU/GPU/TPU)
Efficient factorization algorithm reducing neurosymbolic compute and memory overhead
CogSys ASIC architecture with reconfigurable nsPEs and bubble streaming dataflow
Adaptive workload-aware scheduler enabling real-time abduction reasoning at 0.3s per task in 4mm^2, 1.48W

metrics.speedup: >75x over TPU-like systolic array; 4x-96x over desktop/edge GPUs
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 1.48W power; <5% area overhead vs systolic array baseline

limitations: Evaluation is limited to TSMC 28nm synthesis; real-time performance on production silicon for larger neurosymbolic models is not validated.
primary_theme: Neurosymbolic AI accelerator with reconfigurable compute and adaptive scheduling
